description_en: North temple, part of a five-temples complex from the 14th-15th century.The monument is part of a five-temples complex located to the eastern side of the village of Mānmā, 1 km south and down the hill of Mānmā-Khām̐ḍācakra, the Kalikot district headquarters.The temple occupies the northern part of a quincux plan composed of fiveśikharatemples, locally known asdeval(or 'temple' in Sanskrit). The central temple of the complex is the largest one. The four other, smaller temples, are built one meter away from the central temple, facing its south, west, north and east facades. The four sides of the central temple are each marked by two pillars supporting a small overhanging pediment.The monument has a single door, oriented to the south. In front of it are the two pillars of the central temple's reduced porch (Skt.ardhamaṇḍapa). The door lintel is richly decorated with low-relief carvings of spirales, rosettes. At the centre of the lintel is an anthropomorphic character holding what appears to be a trident, which may identify it as Śiva. Inside the sanctum is a stoneyoni, without itsśivaliṅga. The room is covered by a corbelled vault. To the right of the door is a low-relief carving of a seated character with its hands joined in front of the torso.On top of the monument are two stoneāmalakadiscs surmounted by an ogival pinnacle.Thepañcadevalaplan is mostly found in the districts of Dailekh, Achham and Kalikot, which correspond to the area controlled by the Rāskoṭi kings. This dynasty ruled between the end of the 14th century and the end of the 18th century. Furthermore, the construction ofśikharatemples in the Karnali region seems to have stopped before the 16th century, which narrows the dating of this type of plan down to the 14th-15th century.The site is mentioned inSharma 1972: 23, 25, 32;Sharma 2012: 198-199 andAndolfatto 2019: 201-214.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
